h1: What has Indian research actually found on Kappaphycus and Gracilaria sap?
title: Kappaphycus and Gracilaria sap: Indian research | GBO
desc: What CSIR-CSMCRI, ICAR and Indian field trials reported on K-sap and G-sap, and what a marketer can and cannot conclude from it.
answer: Indian field trials report that foliar Kappaphycus and Gracilaria sap improved growth and yield in maize and in a rice-potato-blackgram sequence. An ICAR wheat study reports better drought response with Kappaphycus extract. CSIR-CSMCRI work points to photosynthesis and hormone genes. Marketers can say sap has been studied. They cannot promise those results for any product.
sections: what-was-tested
What Indian researchers actually tested

K-sap and G-sap are the common short names for sap from Kappaphycus alvarezii and Gracilaria edulis. CSIR-CSMCRI developed a route that liquefies fresh seaweed into a sap and recovers carrageenan from what is left. The studies below are ones we opened and read. They are not a complete review.

StudyMaterialCrop and setupDirection reported
Singh and co-workers, Journal of Applied Phycology, 2016K-sap and G-sap, 2.5 to 15%Rain-fed maize, field, 18 treatments, full or half fertiliser rateGrain yield rose at the best doses. G-sap raised grain P and K.
Basavaraja and co-workers, Journal of Plant Nutrition, 2018K-sap and G-sap, 2.5 to 15%, three foliar spraysHybrid maize, field, rabi 2011 to 2013, Mandya, KarnatakaGrain yield and nutrient uptake rose at 10% against a water spray.
Layek and co-workers, Indian Journal of Agronomy, 2016K-sap and G-sap, 5% and 10% foliar, plus seed soakMaize, two kharif seasons, ICAR centre at Umiam, MeghalayaHeight, dry matter and chlorophyll rose. Leaf temperature fell.
Pramanick and co-workers, Indian Journal of Agronomy, 2018K-sap and G-sap, 2.5 to 15%Rice-potato-blackgram sequence, field, 2011 to 2013, Nadia, West BengalYield, uptake and returns generally rose with concentration. Some yield traits did not differ.
Meena and co-workers, ICAR-IARI, Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 2026Kappaphycus extract from a commercial concentrate, 2.5 to 10% foliarWheat, two rabi seasons, New Delhi, 10-day droughtBetter water status and membrane stability. Shoot biomass highest at 10%.
Trivedi and co-workers, CSIR-CSMCRI, Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems, 2021Kappaphycus extract, 10% foliarMaize in net-house pots, water withheldGreen cob yield and photosynthesis were higher. Gene activity shifted.
Vaghela and co-workers, CSIR-CSMCRI, Frontiers in Plant Science, 2023Minimally processed Kappaphycus and Sargassum homogenatesMaize in net-house pots, one rabi run at BhavnagarBoth doses improved growth and yield, generally best at the lower dose.

For how these species differ as raw materials, see our species comparison. This guide is only about the research record.
where-studies-agree
Where the studies agree, and where they do not

They agree on direction. In each study above, sap or extract did better than its control on at least some measures. Four of the field trials tested both Kappaphycus and Gracilaria side by side, so the Gracilaria record sits mostly inside those trials.

We did not open an Indian study reporting no benefit. That does not prove none exists, so treat this set as a sample.

They do not agree on dose:

  • Singh's best maize treatments were 5% G-sap or 7.5% K-sap with full fertiliser.
  • Basavaraja's result was at 10%.
  • Layek found two sprays of 10% were needed for a significant gain in net returns. It also found that soaking seed in 5% sap helped germination, while 10% and 15% reduced it.
  • Pramanick reported little yield improvement going from 2.5% to 5%, with gains mainly at 10% or more.
  • Vaghela's pot trial generally did best at the lower of its two doses.

So there is no single research-backed rate to quote. Rate depended on crop, method and study.
what-mechanism-work-shows
What the mechanism work shows

Trivedi's CSIR-CSMCRI study looked at maize leaves under drought. Treated plants showed changes in genes tied to cytokinin, gibberellin, abscisic acid, nitrogen use and photosynthesis. The authors present this as a working picture and say further validation of individual genes is needed.

Vaghela's team profiled the homogenates and listed candidate compounds. These were tentative database matches, and the authors say effective concentrations still need to be measured. The ICAR-IARI wheat abstract reports lower electrolyte leakage and hydrogen peroxide under drought.

The fair summary: the work points to plausible pathways. It does not identify one active ingredient that a label could stand on.
why-not-a-product-claim
Why a study is not a product claim

• Percentages do not transfer. A "10% sap" spray is a dilution of that study's own sap. A grade name states a product specification. In Vaghela's trial, 10% and 20% sprays equalled only 0.35% and 0.7% on a total solids basis. Compare solids, not headline numbers.
  • The material differs. The CSIR route starts from fresh seaweed and says the sap may be marketed directly once preservatives are added. A concentrate, powder, granule or blend is a different material that these trials did not test.
  • Setups differ. Net-house pots are not fields. Rain-fed Meghalaya maize is not irrigated rabi maize in Mandya. Most trials cover one site and a few seasons.
  • Check who is behind the paper. Singh's work acknowledges CSIR support. Vaghela's author list includes a private seaweed company. The ICAR-IARI study used a commercial concentrate. None of this makes a result wrong, but readers should know it.
what-you-can-say
What a marketer can and cannot say

Reasonable to sayNot supported by these papers
Kappaphycus and Gracilaria sap have been tested in Indian field trials on maize and a rice-based sequence.Our product gives the yield rise reported in a paper.
Named studies reported improved growth or yield against their controls, at stated doses.Sap works on every crop, soil or season.
CSIR-CSMCRI work links Kappaphycus extract to changes in photosynthesis and hormone-related genes in maize.We know exactly which compound causes the effect.
Some trials combined sap with reduced fertiliser and reported results worth studying.Sap replaces fertiliser, or lets a farmer cut a set share of it.
A named species was the material studied.This paper proves our grade, blend, powder or granule works.

Research also does not settle legal status. Biostimulants are regulated under clause 20C of the Fertiliser Control Order, brought in by S.O. 882(E) of 23 February 2021. Provisional registrations have been invalid since 17 June 2025. As of September 2025, Schedule VI held 146 products. Later amendments may have added more, so read the latest Gazette list and our Schedule VI overview. A published paper does not place a product on that list. Check with your state agriculture department.
raw-material
Where the raw material comes from

A 2024 National Academy of Agricultural Sciences paper gives the clearest picture we could open. Commercial Kappaphycus farming is primarily in Tamil Nadu, with average annual production of 5,200 tonnes fresh weight. Farmed Gracilaria edulis is about 60 tonnes wet weight a year. Wild collection of all seaweeds is about 52,000 tonnes wet weight. The paper calls good seed material a primary requisite for farming.

Government support is growing. The PMMSY target in that paper is 1.12 million tonnes wet weight within five years. A Lok Sabha reply of February 2025 lists 47,245 rafts and 65,480 monoline or tubenet units approved. Approved units are not harvested tonnes.

Kappaphycus is cultivated and harvested for its carrageenan content, so sap and carrageenan can draw on the same harvest. For Gracilaria, farmed volumes in the NAAS figures are very small. If a product leans on Gracilaria research, ask for species and origin documents.
what-we-can-add
What we can add as a manufacturer

We make seaweed extract at our own plant at GIDC Shihor, Bhavnagar, with capacity of 100 KL liquid and 2,500 t solid a month. We have worked with farmers since 2006 and hold Gujarat NOCs for 36 FCO Schedule VI biostimulant grades and 11 biofertiliser types. Our seaweed extraction is mild and in-house, without harsh chemicals, very high pH or heat.

Our listed Kappaphycus grades are 24%, 9.5% and 7.2% liquid, plus a 1:1 Kappaphycus and Sargassum swartzii liquid. We list no Gracilaria grade. We do not offer the papers above as proof for any of our grades. Judge any supplier's material, including ours, on its own specification and your own trials.
faq: Does Indian research show that K-sap increases yield?

Several Indian trials reported higher yield or growth with K-sap against their controls, mostly in maize and a rice-based sequence. Those results belong to the sap, dose and site tested. They are not a promise for any product.
Is Gracilaria sap as well studied as Kappaphycus sap?
Gracilaria sap appears in several Indian field trials alongside Kappaphycus. The mechanism papers we opened used Kappaphycus, so less is shown about how Gracilaria sap acts.
Can I print a research yield figure on my label or brochure?
Avoid it. A figure from a trial describes that trial's material, dose, crop and season. For what a label may say, check the current FCO rules and check with your state agriculture department.
Does a 10% sap spray equal a 10% seaweed grade?
No. In trials, the percentage is a dilution of the sap used. One CSMCRI trial showed 10% spray volume equalled 0.35% on a total solids basis. A grade name is a product specification.
Is enough Kappaphycus and Gracilaria grown in India?

A 2024 NAAS paper gives about 5,200 tonnes fresh weight of farmed Kappaphycus a year, and about 60 tonnes wet weight of farmed Gracilaria edulis. Later figures may differ, so confirm supply with documents from your supplier.
audience: Marketers, brand owners, dealers, blenders, co-operatives, importers and agronomists
